summary: Small missing credit on finalized invoice after overnight batch crossed DST boundary - microbatch rounding gap
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a small unexpected deduction (USD 0.73) on their finalized invoice after a scheduled overnight batch embedding job. The job spanned the DST transition (spring forward) and appears to have been split across two hourly metering windows. Impact:
- Finalized invoice shows a missing credit line of $0.73 relative to provisional credit estimate provided before finalization.
- Customer requests explanation, audit trail, and whether this is refundable.
Environment:
- prod, us-east-1 region
- Customer keys: sk_live_xxx (provided in secure channel)
- Job type: multi-file batch embeddings (async) using microbatch size 128, scheduled 2026-03-14 01:45 - 03:10 local time (DST shift at 02:00)
- Model: text-embedding-3-large

Why this is unusual:
Hourly smoothing and microbatch aggregation normally round per-hour credits. The customer claims the rounding/truncation behavior after the DST boundary produced a lost fractional credit (0.73 USD) rather than being carried or smoothed as expected.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Schedule an async multi-file embedding job that crosses DST boundary in a US region (e.g., start 01:45 local time, end 03:10 local time on DST start day).
2) Use microbatch size 128 and ensure split across the hourly postback window (we saw microbatches finishing ~01:59:58 and next at 02:00:04 local).
3) Allow hourly postback aggregator + hourly smoothing job to run and finalize invoice for the billing cycle.
4) Compare provisional credits shown in console prior to invoice finalization against the finalized invoice line items.
logs: Customer-provided postback payloads (timestamps redacted) attached to secure channel: batch_postback_20260314_01.json, batch_postback_20260314_02.json
Scheduler trace: scheduler.job_id=ae3f2c, microbatch completions at 01:59:58 and 02:00:04 local
Postback processor logs: billing/postback-processor/2026-03-14.log lines 1203-1222 show two postbacks placed in adjacent hourly buckets
Hourly smoother run: hourly-smoothing/run-2026-03-14-03:00.log indicates rounding_policy=truncate (current default)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 17:10 - Support (Lena): Initial triage, confirmed customer invoice and provisional estimate differ by USD 0.73. Requested secure upload of postbacks and scheduler traces.
2026-03-13 19:05 - Customer (BrightFAQ): Uploaded anonymized postbacks and job id. Provided time zone: America/New_York. Confirmed batch ran during spring-forward DST transition.

2026-03-13 21:30 - Billing eng (Marcus): Replayed postbacks in staging aggregator. Observed microbatch completion timestamps falling into two different hourly buckets because clock jumped forward at 02:00 local. Aggregator attributed partial microbatch token counts to previous hour and remainder to next hour.

2026-03-13 22:10 - Billing eng (Marcus): Found hourly_smoother configured with rounding_policy=truncate; smoothing algorithm truncates fractional credits per-hour after smoothing which can produce small losses when buckets are split across DST (edge case).

2026-03-14 09:00 - SRE (Priya Raman): Confirmed system clock behavior: nodes follow host TZ and scheduler microbatch completion times are wall-clock-based; postback timestamps are trusted. No evidence of duplicate postbacks or missing tokens.
impact_summary: Customer lost USD 0.73 due to truncation in hourly smoothing when a batch spanned a DST boundary and microbatches were split across hours. No other customers in sample run exhibited >$5 variance; this is a small, user-facing billing discrepancy but important to customer trust.
customer_communication: 2026-03-13 20:00 - Support (Lena): Acknowledged report and requested postback payloads and scheduler traces. Promised initial update within SLA window.

2026-03-14 10:30 - Support (Marcus): Explained preliminary findings: smoothing algorithm truncates fractional credits per hour, which led to the observed $0.73 gap when the job crossed DST. Offered provisional credit and said we'll propose a fix to avoid future occurrences.

2026-03-14 11:00 - Customer (BrightFAQ, Customer Success): Appreciative of quick root cause. Requests a credit and notes this affects accounting reconciliation for their finance team. Asked for a permanent mitigation timeline.
2026-03-14 15:00 - Support (Lena): Committed to issuing a one-time adjustment for USD 0.73 and to follow up with Engineering for a mitigation plan.
resolution_notes: Workaround/fix: Issued a one-time credit of USD 0.73 to BrightFAQ Inc. (internal billing credit ref BILL-ADJ-624999). Short-term mitigation: modify hourly_smoother to use rounding_policy=round_half_up for any buckets affected by timezone/DST splits for next billing run (target PR and canary for 2026-03-20). Long-term: engineering will adopt cumulative fractional carryover across adjacent hourly buckets as part of the hourly smoothing redesign (tracked in internal ticket INT-20412).
resolution: Provisional credit issued; engineering patch scheduled for canary and metrics monitoring added. Customer notified and accepted credit; ticket moved to monitoring pending deployment.

next_steps: 1) Billing Eng will merge and canary PR to modify rounding_policy for DST-split windows (PR 1987). Target canary date 2026-03-20.
2) Product/Billing to update runbook to carry fractional credit between adjacent hourly buckets rather than per-hour truncation (tracked in INT-20412).
3) Support to confirm credit appears on customer's next bank/invoice and close ticket after one confirmation cycle.
4) Add automated detection for jobs that span DST boundary and emit a warning in console to recommend aligning scheduled jobs or switching to continuous-hour aggregation.
